_meta.description: Inchworm roster (canonical). Edit this file, then run `python3 scripts/build_page.py` to regenerate index.html's data layer. benchmarked = the 'Benchmarked' tab rows; pending = the 'Pending Eval' tab (newer models, no comparable scores yet); candidates_no_benchmarks is a discovery pool never rendered.
_meta.local_eval_is: HumanEval+ from our own runs: plain chatml, greedy, official EvalPlus evaluator
_meta.build: index.html data consts generated by scripts/build_page.py

benchmarked.name: Qwen3-8B
benchmarked.best: The current Local eval leader — a general model that out-codes every coder-tuned 8B on HumanEval+.
benchmarked.note: HumanEval+ and HumanEval entirely from our own self-evaluated run on this machine (plain chat template with thinking disabled, greedy, official EvalPlus evaluator): 81.1 / 85.4. No feed or card coverage exists, so there is no BigCodeBench value yet. A general (hybrid-thinking) model, not code-tuned — which makes the score more notable. ~10 min/sample in bf16 on MPS; allow a multi-hour run.

benchmarked.name: Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct
benchmarked.best: The top rung for local coding — only when you have 24GB+ to spare.
benchmarked.note: Highest scores on this page, from the Qwen2.5-Coder technical report (HumanEval+ 75.9, HumanEval 84.1). Smooth on 24GB+ unified-memory Macs or 24GB VRAM laptops (~45-60 tok/s at Q4); on 16GB machines it gets tight.

benchmarked.name: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct
benchmarked.best: A balanced daily driver for Python, JS, and debugging.
benchmarked.note: Strong general-purpose coding model with a large context window. The instruct variant is especially useful for iterative edits.

benchmarked.name: Yi-Coder-9B-Chat
benchmarked.best: High scores with strong multilingual code support.
benchmarked.note: One of the best sub-10B models for code. Excels at long-context tasks and supports a wide range of languages.

benchmarked.name: DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-Instruct
benchmarked.best: A proven older model with broad tooling support.
benchmarked.note: Still practical in local runtimes thanks to its mature GGUF ecosystem and reasonable memory footprint.

benchmarked.name: StarCoder2-7B
benchmarked.best: A transparent, permissively licensed baseline.
benchmarked.note: A solid open code model and useful reference point. It tends to benefit from precise prompts and a little more scaffolding.

benchmarked.name: Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct
benchmarked.best: Fast local completions on compact machines.
benchmarked.note: The smallest model in this set, but surprisingly capable for routine code generation, transformations, and lightweight agents.

benchmarked.name: Phi-3.5-mini-instruct
benchmarked.best: Low-memory coding assistance and quick iteration.
benchmarked.note: Compact and efficient. It is better suited to focused tasks than large multi-file refactors.

benchmarked.name: CodeGemma-7B-it
benchmarked.best: A dependable Google-weighted baseline.
benchmarked.note: Good for code completion and explanation workflows. Check the license and usage terms before shipping it inside a product.

benchmarked.name: CodeLlama-7b-Instruct
benchmarked.best: A well-known baseline, though outperformed by newer models.
benchmarked.note: Pioneer code model. Still widely used but clearly surpassed by Qwen and DeepSeek in recent benchmarks.

benchmarked.name: Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct
benchmarked.best: Tiny model that still produces usable code.
benchmarked.note: Impressive for its size. Great for quick completions, autocomplete, and resource-constrained environments. Our self-evaluated HumanEval+ run (59.8) actually came in slightly above the card-reported 56.8.

benchmarked.name: StarCoder2-3B
benchmarked.best: Lightweight open model for constrained hardware.
benchmarked.note: The smallest StarCoder2 variant. Good for embedded or mobile code-assist scenarios.

benchmarked.name: Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct
benchmarked.best: General-purpose small model that codes respectably.
benchmarked.note: Not code-specific, but handles coding tasks well enough for a mixed-use local assistant.

benchmarked.name: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
benchmarked.best: Fast general assistant with decent code ability.
benchmarked.note: Primarily a general chat model. Code performance is acceptable but not its strength.

benchmarked.name: CodeQwen1.5-7B-Chat
benchmarked.best: The benchmark splitter: tops HumanEval+ yet mid-pack on BigCodeBench.
benchmarked.note: A 2024 Qwen coder that still posts the highest HumanEval+ here — proof that HumanEval saturates. BigCodeBench, which needs real library skill, ranks it mid-pack; that contrast is the reason this page pairs both benchmarks.

benchmarked.name: OpenCoder-8B-Instruct
benchmarked.best: The strongest fully-open coder under 10B on BigCodeBench.
benchmarked.note: Infly released weights and training data — a genuinely open code model. On BigCodeBench it sits just below Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, and it leads this page on HumanEval+. Runs comfortably on a 16GB laptop.

benchmarked.name: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
benchmarked.best: The ubiquitous general 8B — a reality check for coding claims.
benchmarked.note: Not code-specialized, but it is the model most people actually run locally. BigCodeBench drops it below every code-tuned model here — a fair view of how general chat models handle real library APIs.

benchmarked.name: Phi-4
benchmarked.best: The reasoning-flavored 14B that redefined "small" — Microsoft's most capable open model.
benchmarked.note: A Dec 2024 generalist with unusual strength in code and math for its size. On BigCodeBench it ranks second here — behind only the code-specialized Qwen 14B — despite not being tuned for code. 14.7B total params, 16K context, MIT license. HumanEval from the model card; no strict HumanEval+ run exists.

benchmarked.name: DeepCoder-14B-Preview
benchmarked.best: The fully-open 14B billed as an o3-mini-level local coder.
benchmarked.note: Apr 2025 preview: an RL-trained agentic coder built on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B, with weights and the whole RL pipeline open (MIT). Its BigCodeBench instruct score measures direct pass@1 — its agentic/long-horizon strengths show up more in tool-use setups.

benchmarked.name: Magicoder-S-DS-6.7B
benchmarked.best: The synthetic-data pioneer that still holds its own.
benchmarked.note: Dec 2024 (Apache-2.0): the OSS-Instruct recipe behind Magicoder seeded today's synthetic training pipelines. Full HumanEval+ and BigCodeBench coverage, and it keeps up with far newer DeepSeek-Coder builds.

benchmarked.name: OpenCoder-1.5B-Instruct
benchmarked.best: A 1.5B that out-codes several 7B models on BigCodeBench.
benchmarked.note: Fully open — weights, training data, and pipeline. BigCodeBench 34.9 beats every other sub-3B model here and even StarCoder2-7B. HumanEval pair from the OpenCoder model card (EvalPlus run); the Local eval column is our own self-evaluated HumanEval+ run on this machine (58.5, plain chatml, greedy).

benchmarked.name: Qwen3-1.7B
benchmarked.best: The tiny dark horse: a 1.7B posting near-top HumanEval+ (third-party reported).
benchmarked.note: Our local HumanEval+ run (Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B, plain chatml prompt, greedy, MPS, official EvalPlus evaluator) scored 55.5% HumanEval+ / 61.0% HumanEval, versus the SOTA2 third-party claim of 73.6% HumanEval+ / 57.2% MBPP+. The SOTA2 variant/config is unpublished and not independently verified; treat its numbers as directional. Qwen3 cards report LiveCodeBench, not HumanEval.

benchmarked.name: Artigenz-Coder-DS-6.7B
benchmarked.best: A DeepSeek-Coder 6.7B fine-tune that out-scores most 7B coders on HumanEval+.
benchmarked.note: DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B instruction fine-tune from EvalPlus+BigCodeBench feeds (HE+ 72.6, BCB 38.0). Strong single-turn results; smaller community footprint than the majors.

benchmarked.name: OpenCodeInterpreter-DS-6.7B
benchmarked.best: An execution-and-iteration coder: near-top HumanEval+ with a tool-calling design.
benchmarked.note: OpenCodeInterpreter (DS-6.7B) from the M-A-P team — code execution + iterative refinement lineage. Feed-sourced HE+ 72.0 / BCB 37.1.

benchmarked.name: WaveCoder-Ultra-6.7B
benchmarked.best: An early Microsoft code-tune that still posts competitive numbers.
benchmarked.note: WaveCoder-Ultra 6.7B (DeepSeek-Coder base) from Microsoft Research Asia. Feed-sourced HE+ 69.5 / BCB 33.9.

benchmarked.name: CodeGeeX4-All-9B
benchmarked.best: The strongest 9B on BigCodeBench among non-Qwen coders.
benchmarked.note: CodeGeeX4-All-9B (THUDM/Zhipu): fills the BigCodeBench column at 40.0 (Hard 18.9) from the feed; no EvalPlus HumanEval+ run exists, so that cell shows —.

benchmarked.name: Granite-4.2-3B
benchmarked.best: Fresh local eval result.
benchmarked.note: HumanEval scores from local self-evaluation run.

pending.name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B
pending.note: In frozen BigCodeBench feed (38.1 instruct); LiveCodeBench pass@1 53.8 per DeepSeek report

pending.name: Phi-4-reasoning
pending.note: Card reports LiveCodeBench/AIME; HumanEvalPlus 83.5 on phi-4-plus variant

pending.name: Granite-4.2-8B
pending.note: Card reports LiveCodeBench v6 + AIME25; no HumanEval

pending.name: DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B
pending.note: DeepSeek distilled R1-0528 reasoning into Qwen3-8B: card reports AIME24 86.0 / AIME25 76.3 / LiveCodeBench 60.5 — SOTA for open ≤8B at release. No HumanEval+/BigCodeBench comparable run yet.

pending.name: DeepCoder-1.5B-Preview
pending.note: 1.5B sibling of the benchmarked 14B. Card self-reports HumanEval+ 73.0 and LiveCodeBench v5 25.1 — self-reported and unverified, same class as the SOTA2 Qwen3-1.7B claim our run refuted; needs a local run.

pending.name: Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Code
pending.note: Ai2 RL-Zero code model (Dolci-RL-Zero-Code dataset, fully open). No pass@1 numbers published on the card yet — only appears in our newest-model sweep.

pending.name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B
pending.note: Official R1 reasoning distill at 1.5B. Card reports AIME24 28.9 / LiveCodeBench 16.9 / Codeforces 954 — modest but the smallest usable R1 family member.

pending.name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B
pending.note: Official R1 reasoning distill at 7B. Card reports AIME24 55.5 / LiveCodeBench 37.6 / Codeforces 1189. On our run queue alongside the other 8B-class candidates.

candidates_no_benchmarks._note: Flagged non-fits from the 2025-2026 discovery audit (see full context in git history). Never rendered; a model only belongs on the page once it has a verifiable coding pass@1 source.
